title: Soy and Ginger Glazed Salmon
description: Crisp-skinned salmon lacquered in a sticky soy, honey and ginger glaze that reduces in the pan in a couple of minutes. Served with jasmine rice and pak choi cooked in what is left behind.

steps.text: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a small saucepan with the measured water, bring to the boil, then cover with a tight lid and cook on the lowest heat.
Take the rice off the heat and leave it to steam with the lid on until you are ready to serve.
While the rice cooks, stir all the glaze ingredients together in a small bowl. Pat the salmon very dry with kitchen paper, especially the skin.
steps.tip: Dry skin is the difference between crisp and flabby, and it also stops the fish sticking.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Lay the salmon in skin-side down, press each fillet flat with a spatula for the first 10 seconds, then leave it alone until the skin is crisp and the flesh has turned opaque about two-thirds of the way up the sides.

Turn the heat down to medium and flip the salmon. Pour the glaze around the fish and let it bubble, spooning it over the fillets, until it is syrupy and the salmon is just cooked through. Lift the salmon onto warm plates.
steps.tip: The honey catches quickly. If the glaze is thickening too fast, add a tablespoon of water and pull the pan off the heat.

steps.text: Put the pak choi cut-side down in the same pan, add 2 tbsp of water and cover with a lid or a plate. Steam until the stems are just tender, turning once to coat in the sticky pan juices.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve with the salmon and pak choi. Spoon over any glaze left in the pan and scatter with the spring onions and sesame seeds.

equipment: non-stick frying pan with a lid
tips: Fillets of even thickness cook most evenly. For a very thick piece, give the skin side an extra minute.

substitutions.note: makes the dish gluten-free if the tamari is labelled so

storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftover salmon keeps for 1 day in the fridge and is good cold, flaked over rice or salad.
author: Simmer
